To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the re- identification of subjects appearing in front an advertising smart screen is a challenging task but it is feasible with a high degree of accuracy.

(i) the re-identification task is possible with a reasonable accuracy, (ii) it is possible to re-identify users with a high accuracy in presence of a small amount of training data (i.e., few faces per user) and a small amount of testing data, (iii) the proposed approach is able to re-identify the users even in presence of occlusion of the faces, (iv) the proposed approach can be easily integrated in a commercial digital signage system, (v
a good accuracy can be achieved for face re-identification on a real dataset collected for digital signage application.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of face re-identification in digital signage applications where the user appears in front an advertising smart screen.
the problem of face re-identification in a digital signage scenario.
the problem of re-identifying a user that appears in front a smart screen.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, even though the reidentification of users appearing at a digital screen is possible, the proposed system can be considered a proof of concept rather than a fully working system.

, although the re-identification problem in a many-to-many scenario is still an open research issue, a good performance in terms of re-identification accuracy is achievable in the considered application scenario.

, although the re-identification task is still in its early stages, it has the potential of becoming a key component in many applications, such as digital signage, and that it can be effectively addressed with a many-to-many approach.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have proposed a framework for reidentifying users in front a smart advertising screen.
the proposed system can be used to trigger advertising campaigns to the right user and it is able to estimate the audience of a store in terms of number of users, age and gender.
we have shown that it is possible to re-identify people appearing in front a smart screen with an accuracy of about 89%.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed re-identification framework can be employed to trigger specific advertising campaigns to a user when he/she is back to the screen after a time slot.
the proposed approach is able to re-identify the same person with a good accuracy, thus allowing the system to trigger the right advertisement for that person.
a many-to-many approach can be used to re-identify users appearing in front an advertising smart screen, with a good accuracy, even if the system is fed with few face samples.
